The write-ahead log is a record of every operation the database system performed. This is done regardless of whether the operation was completed on disk.

## Step 1: Describe how the write-ahead log works
When a database system receives a request to perform an operation, it first records the operation in the write-ahead log (a log of all operations) and then attempts to complete the operation on disk. If the system crashes before the operation is written to disk, the operation remains in the log and is not committed to the database.

## Step 2: Explain how the database recovers after a crash
When the database system restarts after a crash, it reads through the write-ahead log to determine which operations were pending at the time of the crash. These operations are then reapplied to the database, thus ensuring data consistency.

## Step 3: Highlight the importance of the write-ahead log in ensuring database integrity
The write-ahead log plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the database. It prevents potential data loss by recording all operations before they are committed to the database, and allows the database to recover from failures by replaying the operations recorded in the log.
